messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: allocation-pressure on paged-kv-allocator (sv-alloc-23). Symptoms: gradual mem creep -> container restarts on node gce-infr-07, recent CUDA OOMs in logs. Incident id: INC-2026-1789. Please ack and triage.

devon: acked. I'm looking at node metrics and pods. grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/paged-kv?panelId=7

maria: seeing steady increase in resident set on allocator replicas, small spikes correlate with long seq-length requests. Could be KV cache fragmentation + slow leak rather than single big allocation.

kai: logs from the container show repeated CUDA OOM messages before kube restarts the pod. snip:
```
[2026-03-15T01:04:12Z] runtime: launching attention page
[2026-03-15T01:04:14Z] nvml: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T01:04:14Z] runtime: allocator did not free enough pages, attempted fallback
[2026-03-15T01:04:15Z] kernel: oom-killer: kill process 1823 (allocatord) score 987
```

sarah: @kai can you paste the pod name and last 100 lines of allocator logs? also check dmesg on node for GPU driver hints.

kai: pod is rkd-paged-kv-7d9f4. Last logs show a pattern of small evictions failing and then a large allocation attempt. tail:
```
evict: candidates scanned=2048, freed_pages=12
evict: candidates scanned=4096, freed_pages=0
alloc: request=512MB, available_chunks=0
```

emily: I triggered a probe to reduce incoming traffic to these replicas: moved 30% of routed requests to fallback model-quantized-2 via routing layer. That dropped QPS on the set but latency for those customers rose ~60ms. customer impact: a handful of enterprise customers in eu-west saw temporal 5xxs while their requests routed to saturated fallback.

devon: mitigation plan tried so far:
- toggled allocator debug-evict to true (improved awareness)
- increased eviction aggressiveness: `kv-evictctl --threshold=0.6 --scan-batch=8192`
- scaled up replicas by +2 (kubectl scale sts rkd-paged-kv --replicas=5)
- annotated pods to avoid scheduling on gce-infr-07 for now
Result: reduced immediate restarts but node still showing fragmentation and one remaining container crash last 12m.

maria: suspects allocator slab fragmentation: tiny freed_pages counts indicate meta fragmentation. We should force a compact on the allocator to defragment the slab. There's a debug endpoint: `POST /debug/allocator/compact?confirm=true` — I'm hesitant to run on prod without canary.

kai: canary run on rkd-paged-kv-7d9f4-sim succeeded in staging. Suggest run compact on one live replica during low traffic window, then monitor/rollback.

sarah: agree. Also CPU on node jumped before crash — could be GC thrash. Action: schedule compact on one replica now, leave 30% traffic on fallback for 10m, watch OOM count and dmesg. @devon will coordinate.

devon: executing compact on rkd-paged-kv-7d9f4 now:
```
curl -X POST -u admin:*** https://rkd-paged-kv-7d9f4.internal/debug/allocator/compact?confirm=true
```

emily: compact started — logs show progressive freed_chunks. Monitoring: oom_count=0 in last 3m, pod mem stable. Latency for routed fallback steady. I'll keep 30% redirect for 20m.

maria: good signal. Next steps if compact holds: roll compact to remaining replicas one at a time with gradual traffic drain. If it fails or OOMs persist, plan B: drain gce-infr-07, restart node driver, and provision extra capacity in other zones.

kai: note: there are kernel messages indicating GPU driver fault on gce-infr-07 in last 2 days. Ops should check driver version pinned and recent node image updates.

sarah: customer impact summary for handoff:
- Impact window: 01:04 - ongoing (mitigation in progress)
- Symptom: increased 5xx and latency for subset of model-inference requests; eu-west customers affected during traffic shift
- Root cause suspected: KV cache slab fragmentation combined with frequent small evictions leading to allocator failing to free contiguous pages and triggering large CUDA allocations -> OOM -> container crash
- Mitigation performed: aggressive eviction settings, scaled replicas +2, route 30% traffic to fallback, triggered allocator compact on one replica (successful), annotated node to avoid scheduling on gce-infr-07
- Next actions (owners):
  - devon: rollout compact to remaining replicas (in progress)
  - emily: keep 30% fallback routing for 30m and monitor customer errors
  - kai: open infra ticket to investigate GPU driver faults on gce-infr-07 (TKT-4567)
  - maria: create follow-up for allocator slab defrag feature + automated compact endpoint guardrails

devon: rolling compact to remaining replicas now, will do one at a time with 5m observation windows. If we see >1 OOM during window, I'll pause and escalate to node restart.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-1789 status update: mitigated=partial, severity=SEV2, responders=[devon,maria,kai,emily,sarah]. Handoff scheduled to next shift at 04:00 UTC. Please update the incident doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-1789

sarah: handoff notes added. I'll own postmortem draft after stabilization. Good job team :thumbsup:
